cards.text: When the day of Pentecost comes, Jesus' followers are all together in one place. ALL of them, same room, same time. Friend, I have seen group chats that couldn't agree on a time for a WEEK.
So they're sitting there in the house, nice and quiet. Then, SUDDENLY, a sound comes from heaven and fills the WHOLE house.

cards.question: What is the sound from heaven like?
Along with that sound filling the house, what do Jesus' followers see?
The tongues like flames of fire separate and come to rest on each one of them.

cards.text: Then they are ALL filled with the Holy Spirit. Not most of them, not just the front row, ALL of them.

cards.question: Filled with the Holy Spirit, what do Jesus' followers begin to do?

cards.text: Now, Jerusalem has God-fearing Jews living there from every nation under heaven. EVERY nation, friend, which is a whole lot of different ways to say "good morning."

cards.question: When the sound rings out, a crowd comes together in bewilderment, because each one hears Jesus' followers speaking his own ___.

cards.text: Astounded and amazed, the crowd asks, "Are not all these who are speaking Galileans?" I can hear it now: WAIT, run that back.

cards.question: The crowd can't figure out how each of them is hearing these Galileans in his own native language.

cards.text: Then the crowd runs down where they're all from: Parthians, Medes, Elamites, folks from Mesopotamia to Egypt, visitors from Rome, both Jews and converts to Judaism, Cretans and Arabs. Friend, that is the BIGGEST round of where-are-you-from I have ever heard.

cards.question: In all those languages, the crowd hears these Spirit-filled Galileans telling about the wonders of ___.
Once they hear Jesus' followers speaking, the whole crowd understands right away what it all means.

cards.text: But not everybody in that crowd is impressed, and some of them start mocking. There's ALWAYS one table in the back that thinks it's funnier than the show.

cards.question: What do the mockers in the crowd say about Jesus' followers?

answers.text: They are drunk on new wine

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The question does not identify who "them" are. Without the preceding card, "each one of them" has no clear antecedent; the question needs to name Jesus' followers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on discovering an unseen detail rather than reasoning. Cards 3, 4, 5 and 7 give no sufficient basis for inferring the wind, the flames, the flames resting on each person, or speaking in other tongues; card 16 likewise gives no basis for preferring the drunkenness accusation to the other believable mockeries. These five of nine choice cards exceed the allowed few discovery questions, leaving most of the stop's choices without informed guesses.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
